intro: ERG is Ergo's native currency. You use it to pay other people and to pay transaction fees, and miners receive it as their reward for securing the network.

supply.title: A capped supply
supply.p1: At most 97,739,925 ERG will ever be created — not a single coin more. That number isn't anyone's promise; it's written into the rules that every node enforces. If a block tries to create more ERG than the schedule allows, every node simply throws it away.

chart.title: New ERG created per block
chart.label: ERG issued per block by height
chart.caption: Horizontal axis: block height. Each step drops by 3 ERG and lasts 64,800 blocks (~3 months).

origin.title: Where does ERG come from?
origin.p1: Every newly mined block creates some new ERG. This is the only way ERG comes into existence — no ICO, no pre-mine. All future ERG is already sitting in a special box called the emission box, locked by a contract that only allows exactly the scheduled amount to be withdrawn at each block.
origin.p2: The emission schedule has two phases:
origin.phase1: The first 2 years (525,600 blocks): each block creates 75 ERG, of which 7.5 ERG goes to the development fund (treasury).
origin.phase2: After that: every 64,800 blocks (~3 months), the amount per block drops by 3 ERG, until it reaches zero.
origin.now: Right now (block {{height}}) the emission box releases {{emission}} ERG per block. At block {{next}} (around {{nextDate}}) this drops to {{nextEmission}} ERG. Emission from the emission box ends at block {{end}}, estimated around {{date}}. After that, miners keep receiving 3 ERG per block from the re-emission contract (see below).
origin.nowEnded: Emission from the emission box ended at block {{end}}. Miners now receive 3 ERG per block from the re-emission contract (see below).

reemission.title: Re-emission (EIP-27)
reemission.p1: As the reward shrinks towards zero, what will pay miners? In 2022 the community adopted a rule change called EIP-27 (an “Ergo Improvement Proposal” — the way changes to Ergo's rules are proposed and agreed on). Starting at block 777,217, part of each block's reward (up to 12 ERG) is locked away in a “savings” contract — the re-emission contract — instead of being paid to the miner straight away.
reemission.p2: Once the emission box runs dry, this contract keeps releasing 3 ERG per block to miners, extending the period in which they get paid by many years. The total supply doesn't change — the ERG is just “saved up” for the future.
reemission.now: At the current block, of the {{emission}} ERG created, the miner receives {{reward}} ERG immediately; the rest is locked for the re-emission period.
reemission.nowEnded: The emission box is now empty, so the whole 3 ERG block reward is paid from the re-emission contract.

nano.title: The smallest unit: nanoERG
nano.p1: The blockchain doesn't store decimals. Every value is stored as a whole number of nanoERG:

more.title: Want more detail?
more.text: The technical article <emission>Emission schedule & EIP-27</emission> goes into the exact formulas and how the reward is split between the miner, the treasury and the re-emission contract.
